title: AILA Daily Pulse
description: Rolling list of DailyPulseItem objects fetched by the AILA app. English is canonical. German lives under i18n.de. At most 12 items. Ids and source URLs are never reused. Dates are not in the future.

id.description: Stable URL-safe id. Never reuse an id after an item rolls off the list.

date.description: Publication time in ISO-8601 UTC with millisecond precision, for example 2026-10-04T15:00:00.000Z. Must not be in the future. The UTC calendar date is the id prefix.

readTimeMinutes.description: Positive whole minutes to read the item. The same unit as listenTimeMinutes.

listenTimeMinutes.description: Positive whole minutes to listen to the same item.

hook.description: One sentence under the title. The hook or summaryPoints[0] should say what the thing is. The validator warns if neither does.

headline.description: At most 60 characters. In sentence case, glossary terms stay lowercase common nouns.

summaryPoints.description: Exactly three strings: what the source shows, the limit of that claim, and what to check next. The first point or the hook should define the subject for a beginner.

deepDiveMarkdown.description: Exactly four second-level headings, in order: The Hook, The Core Mechanism, The Trade-off, Practical Takeaway. Aim for about 150-260 words in each section. Glossary terms in this English text are lowercase common nouns.

source.description: Exactly one source: the publisher name and a single https URL. Do not reuse the URL on another item.

name.description: Publisher name, for example TechCrunch or NVIDIA Newsroom.

url.description: Well-formed https URL of that publication. Optional network check: node scripts/validate.mjs --check-urls requires HTTP 200.

deepDiveMarkdown.description: Same four ## headings as the English deep dive. Technical AI terms stay in English.
